topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture outline, learning objectives, and the framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Sustained proliferative signaling and growth pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream signaling cascades drive growth signal autonomy and cell proliferation.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoietic and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: They demonstrate how a failure to undergo terminal differentiation contributes to tumor development in both blood cancers and solid tissue carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, replicative immortality, and growth control recap
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer cells circumvent programmed cell death and replicative senescence through p53 and telomerase regulation before concluding the discussion on growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the biochemical alterations underlying cancer cell metabolism, including aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how developing tumors induce new blood vessel formation to overcome diffusion limits for oxygen and nutrients.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and systemic dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the biological steps, clinical tracking, selective pressures, and genomic features involved in cancer metastasis.

topics.label: Conclusion and final remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It summarizes the core message of the lecture, discusses further reading on the hallmarks framework, and closes the session.
